newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee dips slightly vs fwd dlr, spot quiet.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee dips slightly vs fwd dlr, spot quiet.

text.p: The Indian rupee weakened marginally against the forward dollar in morning trade but was stuck in a narrow range against the spot dollar, dealers said.
In latest deals, December-delivery dollars were quoted at a premium of 0.59/0.61 rupees against Wednesday's close of 0.57/0.59.

"It's a combination of factors," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "There is some profit-taking...some corporates find current levels attractive and are booking forward.. banks are swapping their foreign currency deposits."
"But the next major move will be only if the rupee appreciates above 35.75 per dollar," he said. "Till then forward premiums will trade within a range of around two paise."
In the spot market, the rupee was steady in quiet trade, dealers said.
In latest deals, the rupee was quoted 35.762/767 per dollar, after opening at 35.755/765.
"It has been between 35.7625/7675 for most of the morning," said a dealer. "The market is waiting to see whether the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) comes in to buy dollars."
Dealers said the central bank had not bought dollars till late morning on Thursday.
